chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ali ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:

I asked my brother Musa (peace be upon him) about a man who took a pigeon from the pigeons of the Sanctuary (Haram) to Kufa or another place. He said: 'He must return it. If it dies, he must pay its price and give it in charity.'

key_terms.حَمَامُ الْحَرَمِ: Pigeons of the Sanctuary (specifically those in Mecca)

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for taking a pigeon from the Haram and it dies?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) clarifies the specific compensation (kaffarah) for unlawfully removing a domesticated bird from the Haram's sanctuary, establishing a precedent for protecting the sanctity of sacred spaces. The ruling distinguishes between the obligation of restitution (returning the bird) and financial liability (paying its value as charity if it perishes), reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on preserving the ecological and spiritual integrity of the Haram. This case study is frequently cited in discussions regarding the rights of animals within the boundaries of the two holy mosques.
